items.title: Reorder dirty classifier so declared artifacts cannot override material/fixture/config
items.context: dirty-worktree.ts classifyParsedRow currently checks isDeclaredArtifactPath BEFORE isFixturePath and isMaterialSourcePath. Move the declared check to AFTER material/fixture so a declared path can only rescue rows that would otherwise be unexpected_dirty_files — never reclassify a blocking material_source_changes or fixture_changes row. This is the hard gate against the CRITICAL bypass.

items.title: Reject material/fixture/config/metadata paths at artifact_declare entry
items.context: artifact_declare assertSafePath only blocks glob/absolute/.. — extend it to also reject paths classified as material_source / fixture / config / story-framework-managed metadata (use the same classifier vocabulary). This is fail-fast UX layered on top of the classifier hard gate; both are required so a JSON-injected declared-artifacts.json entry is still caught by the classifier.

items.title: Block uncommitted declared artifacts at the DONE gate
items.context: declared_artifact_changes is blocking:false in dirty-gate-policy so an uncommitted declared artifact passes DONE but git merge will not carry it to main — it vanishes silently. Add a DONE gate row that, for each declared-artifacts.json entry, requires the path to be either committed-and-clean or absent; a dirty/untracked declared path blocks DONE with guidance to commit (deliverable) or remove (temp output). REVIEW/TEST keep the existing non-blocking behavior.

items.title: Regression-cover the full declared-artifact gate-bypass attack chain
items.context: Add smoke coverage proving: artifact_declare --path=packages/main/src/core/store.ts is rejected; a dirty source file declared as artifact still classifies as material_source_changes (blocking); a dirty fixture declared as artifact still classifies as fixture_changes (blocking); an uncommitted declared generated output blocks the DONE gate with commit/cleanup guidance; declared generated output behaves as non-blocking in REVIEW/TEST.
